inline_comments.comment: The Vue (TS) CSF Next snippet filename is changed from `.storybook/preview.ts` to `.storybook/preview.tsx`, but the implementation in `configure.ts` only assigns the `.tsx` extension for `SupportedRenderer.REACT`, `SupportedRenderer.PREACT`, and `SupportedRenderer.REACT_NATIVE`. Vue projects will have `preview.ts`, not `preview.tsx`. This misdocuments the generated filename for Vue users. Other doc files in this same PR (e.g., `storybook-preview-auto-docs-custom-docs-container.md`) correctly change Vue from `.tsx` → `.ts`, showing the intended direction.

Same problem as line 65: the Vue JS snippet is changed from `.storybook/preview.js` to `.storybook/preview.jsx`. Vue projects will have `preview.js`, not `preview.jsx`. Revert to `.storybook/preview.js`.

The Angular (TS) snippet is changed to `.storybook/preview.tsx`. Angular projects are not in the `isJsx` renderer list, so they will continue to generate `preview.ts`. This should remain `.storybook/preview.ts`.

The web-components (TS) snippet is changed to `.storybook/preview.tsx`. Web-components is not in the `isJsx` list in `configure.ts`, so `preview.ts` is the correct generated filename. Revert to `.storybook/preview.ts`.
The web-components (JS) snippet is changed to `.storybook/preview.jsx`. Web-components is not in the `isJsx` list, so the generated file will be `preview.js`. Revert to `.storybook/preview.js`.

`SupportedRenderer.SOLID` and `SupportedRenderer.QWIK` are both valid enum members (they exist in the types package) and both are JSX-based frameworks, yet they are absent from the `isJsx` array. A Solid.js project initialised with this code will generate `preview.ts`/`preview.js`, but Solid templates use JSX syntax, requiring `.tsx`/`.jsx` for TypeScript's JSX transform to apply. The documentation changes in this PR already reflect the `.ts` outcome for Solid (e.g., `decorator-parameterized-in-preview.md`), but the documentation change and the missing renderer entries together leave Solid and Qwik users with a misconfigured preview file. Add `SupportedRenderer.SOLID` and `SupportedRenderer.QWIK` to the array (and update associated docs), or document explicitly why they are excluded.

The text was changed from `.storybook/preview.js|ts` to `.storybook/preview.ts|tsx`, silently dropping the JavaScript (`.js`) option. Non-TypeScript projects are still supported and still generate `preview.js`. The prior phrasing was more accurate; consider `preview.*` or restore the JS variants: `.storybook/preview.js|jsx|ts|tsx`.

The bullet point now reads `.storybook/preview.tsx` (previously `.storybook/preview.ts`). This is only correct for React/Preact/React Native projects. Angular, Vue, Svelte, etc. users reading this API reference will have a `.ts` preview. Use `.storybook/preview.*` (consistent with neighbouring references updated elsewhere in this PR) or restore the more general `.storybook/preview.ts|tsx`.

The `diff` block title is changed from `.storybook/preview.js|ts` to `.storybook/preview.jsx|tsx`. This section documents CSF Next for all renderers (the surrounding text says "replace your-framework with the framework you are using"), so a React-only extension pair in the title is misleading. Use `.storybook/preview.*` or `preview.js|jsx|ts|tsx` as done elsewhere in the docs.

Changed from `.storybook/preview.js|ts` to `.storybook/preview.ts|tsx`, dropping the `.js` JavaScript variant. JavaScript projects are still supported. Restore to `.storybook/preview.js|ts|tsx` or use `preview.*`.

Changed from `preview.js|ts` to `preview.jsx|tsx`, excluding non-React renderers that use plain `.js`/`.ts`. Three other identical occurrences in this file (lines 65, 94, 110) make the same mistake. Use `preview.*` or `preview.js|jsx|ts|tsx` for renderer-agnostic guidance.

`renderer: SupportedRenderer.REACT_NATIVE` is paired with `frameworkPackage: '@storybook/react-vite'`. These two don't correspond to a real project configuration. While the test is only validating the file extension (not the generated content), the unrealistic combination could mislead future readers. Consider using `SupportedRenderer.REACT` with `@storybook/react-vite` to keep the fixture coherent, or add a brief comment noting the `frameworkPackage` value is irrelevant to this assertion.

The code-fence language is changed from ` ```js ` to ` ```jsx ` while the `filename` attribute remains `.storybook/preview.js`. A `.js` filename with a `jsx` fence type is inconsistent and could confuse readers who rely on the filename to know what to create. Either change the filename to `.storybook/preview.jsx` (if Solid is meant to use JSX extensions — see the `configure.ts` concern about Solid) or revert the fence back to ` ```js `.

The filename is changed from `.storybook/preview.tsx` to `.storybook/preview.ts`, but the opening code fence remains ` ```tsx `. The `tsx` syntax highlighter signals JSX content, which is at odds with the `.ts` filename. If Solid should use `.ts`, change the fence to ` ```ts `; if it should keep `.tsx` (because Solid uses JSX), revert the filename.

The `title` attribute on the "Absolute imports" example is changed from `index.jsx|tsx` to `index.tsx`. This strips the JavaScript variant and is unrelated to the goal of renaming the preview file. Next.js projects can have `.jsx` component files too; reverting to `index.jsx|tsx` (or using `index.*`) is more accurate and keeps the scope of this PR focused.

general_comments.comment: `automock-register-mock-file.md` is the only snippet file in this PR that goes in the wrong direction for non-React renderers (Vue, Angular, web-components are changed from `.ts`/`.js` → `.tsx`/`.jsx`). Every other multi-renderer snippet file edited in this PR (e.g., `storybook-preview-auto-docs-custom-docs-container.md`, `storybook-preview-auto-docs-custom-template-function.md`, `storybook-preview-auto-docs-override-mdx-container.md`) correctly changes those same renderers from `.tsx` → `.ts`. The `automock-register-mock-file.md` changes need to be inverted to match the implementation and the rest of the docs.

The PR adopts two different notations for "any valid extension": `preview.*` (used in most prose) and explicit pairs like `preview.ts|tsx` or `preview.js|ts` (used in code titles and some prose). Using `preview.*` consistently throughout prose and `preview.jsx|tsx` (or `preview.js|jsx|ts|tsx`) only where a concrete file extension must be shown in a code block title would make the docs easier to maintain. Currently both forms are mixed even within individual pages.

Doc snippets for Vue, Angular, and web-components that use a `tsx`/`jsx` code-fence but now have a `.ts`/`.js` filename (after the correct corrections elsewhere in this PR) create a syntax-highlighter mismatch. These are snippets whose *content* wraps stories in React components (e.g., `import * as React from 'react'` for the DocsContainer or MDXProvider). If a Vue or Angular user copies this snippet verbatim, they need TypeScript JSX support, which is only enabled in `.tsx` files by default. Consider noting this caveat, or restructuring those snippets to use a React-renderer-only block rather than a Vue/Angular-specific block that happens to embed React.

The `AGENTS.md` note says "TSX for React-based frameworks", but the implementation covers REACT, PREACT, and REACT_NATIVE. Preact is a separate project and is not universally described as "React-based"; the same applies to REACT_NATIVE. A more precise phrasing — "TSX for React, Preact, and React Native" — or a reference to the explicit list would reduce ambiguity for agents reading this file.
